thought.text: All three dev servers are up (app 200, cms 200, boards 200) with 1.2GB still available. Now the complete final verification through the proxy:

reasoning_content:
Excellent! All three dev servers are up:
- app: 200 (on 39001)
- cms: 200 (on 39002)
- boards: 200 (on 39003)
- 1232MB available

Wait — but I need to verify that the ports match the nginx.conf. The sequential startup might have caused port drift again. Let me check:
- app on 39001: this matches (I just started it, and the port was available)
- cms on 39002: matches
- boards on 39003: matches

But wait — when I started app last, ports.json had {app:39001, cms:39002, boards:39003}. app's stored port 39001 was available → app ran on 39001. No drift this time! Let me verify via the proxy.

Actually, I need to re-check: when `just serve --apps=app` started, did it re-allocate ports for cms/boards (the ones that were running on 39002/39003)? In that case ports.json would change, but what matters is nginx.conf, which was rendered with 39001/39002/39003. The actual servers: boards=39003, cms=39002, app=39001 — all match nginx.conf.

Now let me do a final complete verification through the proxy.

action.command:
echo "===== FINAL VERIFICATION $(date +%H:%M) ====="
echo
echo "--- 1. Containers ---"
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}' | sort
echo
echo "--- 2. Frontends via shared proxy (port 80, *.workspace.localhost) ---"
for h in app.workspace.localhost cms.workspace.localhost boards.workspace.localhost; do
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null --max-time 15 -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:80/" -H "Host: $h" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  $h -> $code"
done
echo
echo "--- 3. Backend API (actuator) ---"
docker exec urbo-workspace-spring-app-1 sh -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8081; printf "GET /health HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n" >&3; sleep 1; cat <&3' 2>/dev/null | tail -1
echo
echo "--- 4. Keycloak realm + seeded admin login ---"
curl -sS -o /dev/null --max-time 10 -w "  keycloak realm: %{http_code}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:80/realms/swcode" -H "Host: keycloak.workspace.localhost"
curl -sS --max-time 15 "http://127.0.0.1:80/realms/swcode/protocol/openid-connect/token" -H "Host: keycloak.workspace.localhost" -d "grant_type=password&client_id=urbo-frontend&username=test@test.de&password=test" | node -e 'let d="";process.stdin.on("data",c=>d+=c).on("end",()=>{try{const j=JSON.parse(d);console.log("  admin login (test@test.de): access_token="+!!j.access_token+", type="+j.token_type+", ttl="+j.expires_in+"s")}catch(e){console.log("  login parse: "+d.slice(0,100))}})'
